sentences.text: Angolasaurus is an extinct genus of mosasaur known as the "Angola lizard."
This animal possessed a tail fluke, forward-lying nostrils, and keeled scales to aid in swimming.
It is one of the few Turonian mosasaurs known to have a transatlantic distribution.
CT scans of the type skull and a new skull revealed detailed interior braincase structures.
The genus Angolasaurus was first named by Miguel Telles Antunes in 1964.
Antunes originally described the genus based on a partial skull and skeleton found in 1964.
In 1994, the species was synonymized with Platecarpus bocagei by Lingham-Soliar.
Fieldwork conducted between 2005 and 2009 uncovered at least two new skeletons of Angolasaurus.
Two individuals from the Eagle Ford Formation of Texas were assigned to Angolasaurus in 2007.
Researchers hypothesize that Angolasaurus had dark dorsal patterning to help with thermoregulation due to cooling sea temperatures.
Angolasaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
The animal is classified as a reptile.
The parent group of Angolasaurus is Russellosaurina.
Recent analyses place Angolasaurus in a basal position within the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
Angolasaurus is considered basal to the clade containing Tylosaurinae and Plioplatecarpinae but belongs to neither subfamily.
Fossils of Angolasaurus date from the Turonian to the Coniacian stages.
Remains of Angolasaurus have been found in Angola, the United States, Brazil, and Niger.
The species Angolasaurus bocagei is known exclusively from the Itombe Formation.
Angolasaurus fossils from the Dukamaje Formation consist of vertebrae from individuals of different growth stages.
Angolasaurus fossils have been recovered from the Eagle Ford Formation in Texas.
It is debated whether Angolasaurus fossils from the United States, Brazil, and Niger definitively belong to this genus.
